Hydrogen-powered flight

The RJS-H1 uses electric lift for take-off and hydrogen fuel-cell power for fixed-wing cruise.

Technology / Propulsion

Electric lift.
Hydrogen cruise.

Battery power lifts the RJS-H1 vertically. Once the wing carries its weight, the hydrogen fuel cell supplies power for cruise.

Inside the platform
TechnologyHydrogen propulsion

Inside the platform

Why we fly
on hydrogen.

Raj’s background in industrial gas engineering led to an aircraft powered by a hydrogen fuel cell. Three elements shape its flight.

01

Fuel-cell cruise

A fuel cell supplies steady electrical power for forward flight. Its outputs include water vapour and heat.

02

Electric lift

A compact battery supports the short bursts of power needed for vertical take-off and landing.

03

Fixed-wing flight

Once airborne, the wing carries the aircraft through cruise, extending its time in the air.
